chapter.title: What Makes a Custom Hook
chapter.description: The naming rule, what gets shared and what does not.

blocks.text: A custom hook is a function whose name begins with `use` and which calls other hooks. That is all. There is no special API and no registration - it is a plain function that happens to follow the rules of hooks.
Why the name has to start with use

The prefix is how both React's linter and other developers know the function may call hooks, and therefore that the rules of hooks apply to it. Without the prefix the lint rules cannot check your calls.
Naming a hook `getWindowWidth` compiles fine and then silently breaks the exhaustive-deps and rules-of-hooks checks. Stick to the prefix.
Every component that calls a hook gets its own independent state. Two components using `useWindowWidth` each have their own `width` and their own listener.

blocks.code:
function A() { const width = useWindowWidth(); }  // its own state
function B() { const width = useWindowWidth(); }  // a separate state

blocks.text: If two components genuinely need to share the *same* value, that is a job for lifting state up, context, or a store - not a custom hook.

items: Call hooks at the top level - never inside a condition, loop or nested function.
Call them only from components or from other custom hooks.
The order of hook calls must be identical on every render.

blocks.text: The usual path is: write the logic inside a component first, then move it out when a second component needs it - or when the component gets hard to read.
Return an array or an object?

items: **Array** when there are one or two values the caller will want to rename, like `useState`.
**Object** when there are several, so callers destructure by name and the order does not matter.

blocks.code:
const [value, setValue] = useToggle(false);      // array: names are chosen by caller
const { user, isLoading, error } = useUser(id);  // object: self-documenting

blocks.text: A hook that fetches data, tracks scroll position and writes to localStorage is three hooks. Small hooks compose; large ones only get larger.
A custom hook can call other custom hooks. Building `useUserPosts` on top of `useUser` and `usePosts` is normal and keeps each piece testable.
